Use this procedure to investigate what a fitted model does when selected parameters change. It loads saved baselines, simulates both the baseline and controlled changes on the same selected lists, and saves responses and comparisons.

This is a mechanism check: other parameters retain their fitted values. A parameter change may alter behavior while making the model fit the observations less well. To ask how well a different specification can fit after all free parameters adapt, use the fitting procedure instead.

For input conventions, see the data guide.

Configure this run

Replace fit_paths with the baselines you want to investigate. A sweep names a baseline through fit, one parameter, and its values; each value is applied to a fresh copy of that baseline. Separate sweeps do not form a Cartesian product.

Use parameter_interventions for a named set of simultaneous overrides to one baseline. For example, two mechanism switches can be changed together while every other parameter stays fixed. Choose values appropriate to the model, and keep a separate output folder for each investigation. experiment_count and simulation_seed control repeated simulation, not fitting.

Keep all editable settings in this tagged cell. Later cells derive paths and selections after any Papermill overrides.

1 — Configure baselines and parameter interventions 
# Inputs and saved results — change these for your project.
project_root = None  # Explicit folder, enclosing Git root, or current directory.
data_path = "data/Dupertuys2026.h5"
output_dir = "results/parameter_shifting"

# Models and saved fits — names connect specifications, labels and outputs.
fit_paths = {
    "CMR": "data/fits/Dupertuys2026_CMR_demo.json",
    "eCMR_source_only": "data/fits/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_source_only.json",
    "eCMR_broad": "data/fits/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_broad.json",
}
model_labels = {
    "CMR": "CMR",
    "eCMR_source_only": "Source-only eCMR",
    "eCMR_broad": "Broader eCMR",
}

# Observation selection — queries use fields in your dataset.
trial_query = None
max_subjects = 0  # Zero keeps all participants; a positive value selects the first IDs.
subject_indices = []

# Scientific settings — choose these for the question you are asking.
parameter_sweeps = {
    "CMR_encoding": {
        "fit": "CMR",
        "parameter": "encoding_drift_rate",
        "values": [0.2, 0.5, 0.8],
    },
    "eCMR_source_only_encoding": {
        "fit": "eCMR_source_only",
        "parameter": "encoding_drift_rate",
        "values": [0.2, 0.5, 0.8],
    },
    "eCMR_broad_encoding": {
        "fit": "eCMR_broad",
        "parameter": "encoding_drift_rate",
        "values": [0.2, 0.5, 0.8],
    },
    "temporal_emotional_modulation": {
        "fit": "eCMR_broad",
        "parameter": "phi_emot_modulates_temporal",
        "values": [False, True],
    },
}
parameter_interventions = {}

# Fitting and simulation — optimizer controls are separate from model parameters.
experiment_count = 10
simulation_seed = 2
enable_x64 = True

# Uncertainty and optional behavioral summaries.
confidence_level = 0.95
plot_seed = 0
comparison_analysis_configs = [
    {"target": "jaxcmr.analyses.spc.plot_spc", "title": "Recall by study position"},
    {
        "target": "jaxcmr.analyses.pnr.plot_pnr",
        "title": "First recall",
        "kwargs": {"query_recall_position": 0},
    },
    {
        "target": "jaxcmr.analyses.crp.plot_crp",
        "title": "Temporal transitions",
        "kwargs": {"max_lag": 5},
    },
    {
        "target": "jaxcmr.analyses.cat_recall_rate.plot_cat_recall_rate",
        "title": "Category recall within mixed lists",
        "contrast_name": "Item category",
        "trial_query": "data['list_type'] == 1",
        "kwargs": {
            "category_field": "valence",
            "category_values": [-1, 0],
            "category_labels": ["Emotional", "Neutral"],
            "valid_field": "pres_itemnos",
        },
    },
]
single_analysis_configs = []
analysis_trial_query = "jnp.all(data['pres_itemnos'] > 0, 1)"
filter_repeated_recalls = False
redo_figures = True

# Output overrides and appearance — None uses the default location or style.
figure_dir = None
figure_str = "model_and_data"  # Empty displays figures without saving.
figure_formats = ["png"]
figure_size = (10, 4.8)

Prepare the environment and inputs

Run the following setup cells once, then continue in order. The short installation cell runs only in Colab; local and Slurm runs use the environment you selected during Setup.

project_root anchors relative paths. When it is unset, Colab uses the current directory; elsewhere the notebook uses the enclosing Git project if present, or the current directory. Check the printed location. copy_example_inputs copies requested bundled examples there, reuses matching files, and refuses to overwrite conflicting files. Custom input paths remain your responsibility.

3 — Import packages 
import json

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np

import jaxcmr
from jaxcmr import repetition
from jaxcmr.examples import copy_example_inputs
from jaxcmr.models import model_factory_from_paths
from jaxcmr.fitting import parameters_for_subjects
from jaxcmr.dataset import generate_trial_mask
from jaxcmr.helpers import import_from_string
from jaxcmr.helpers import load_data, save_dict_to_hdf5
from jaxcmr.helpers import resolve_project_path, resolve_project_root
from jaxcmr.plotting import save_figure
from jaxcmr.plotting import iter_analysis_figures
from jaxcmr.simulation import simulate_dataset

Feature composition stays explicit here. feature_column selects the categorical feature, and concat_features=True combines categorical columns before semantic columns. When concatenation is requested, supply both feature arrays; otherwise the configured concatenation fails rather than substituting a different feature set.

4 — Define feature loading and model construction 
def load_features(spec):
    if spec.get("concat_features", False):
        semantic = np.load(resolve_project_path(spec["embedding_path"], root_path))
        categorical = np.load(
            resolve_project_path(spec["emotion_feature_path"], root_path)
        )[:, int(spec.get("feature_column", 6)) : int(spec.get("feature_column", 6)) + 1]
        return np.concatenate([categorical, semantic], axis=1)
    semantic = np.load(resolve_project_path(spec["embedding_path"], root_path)) if spec.get("embedding_path") else None
    categorical = (
        np.load(resolve_project_path(spec["emotion_feature_path"], root_path))[
            :,
            int(spec.get("feature_column", 6)) : int(spec.get("feature_column", 6)) + 1,
        ]
        if spec.get("emotion_feature_path")
        else None
    )
    return categorical if categorical is not None else semantic


def construct_model(spec):
    return model_factory_from_paths(spec["model_factory"], spec["components"])
5 — Load observations and establish runtime settings 
root_path = resolve_project_root(project_root)
print("Project directory:", root_path)

copy_example_inputs([data_path, *fit_paths.values()], base_dir=root_path)

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", enable_x64)
data_path = resolve_project_path(data_path, root_path)
output_dir = resolve_project_path(output_dir, root_path)
output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
data = load_data(str(data_path))
data_source = (
    data_path.relative_to(root_path).as_posix()
    if data_path.is_relative_to(root_path)
    else str(data_path)
)
subjects = np.asarray(data["subject"]).ravel()

Inspect the baselines and selections

The saved fits supply model components, fitted values and the observation selection. Check that the baseline corresponds to the question you want to investigate before choosing interventions. A pooled baseline and a collection of participant estimates make different claims about individual variation.

Feature loading and model construction remain visible so you can inspect what is reconstructed from each record.

6 — Load baseline fits and select their observations 
fit_paths = {name: resolve_project_path(path, root_path) for name, path in fit_paths.items()}
records = {name: json.loads(path.read_text()) for name, path in fit_paths.items()}
if not records:
    raise ValueError("Supply at least one saved fit.")
display_labels = {
    name: model_labels.get(name, record.get("label", name))
    for name, record in records.items()
}
selections = {}
for name, record in records.items():
    if record.get("data_path", data_source) != data_source:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: the fit refers to a different observation file.")
    if trial_query is None and "selected_trial_indices" in record:
        mask = (
            jnp.zeros(len(subjects), dtype=bool)
            .at[jnp.asarray(record["selected_trial_indices"], dtype=int)]
            .set(True)
        )
    else:
        mask = generate_trial_mask(
            data,
            trial_query
            if trial_query is not None
            else record.get("trial_query", record.get("data_query")),
        )
    subject_ids = np.unique(subjects)
    if max_subjects:
        subject_ids = subject_ids[:max_subjects]
    if subject_indices:
        subject_ids = subject_ids[np.asarray(subject_indices, dtype=int)]
    mask &= jnp.isin(data["subject"].ravel(), subject_ids)
    if not record.get("pooled", record["fits"]["subject"] == [-1]):
        mask &= jnp.isin(
            data["subject"].ravel(), jnp.asarray(record["fits"]["subject"])
        )
    if not bool(mask.any()):
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: no observations match the selected work unit.")
    selections[name] = mask
    print(display_labels[name], "—", int(mask.sum()), "lists; fit:", fit_paths[name])

Simulate baselines and interventions

The next cells build named variants, then simulate the unchanged baseline and each intervention. Unspecified parameters retain baseline values; no optimizer compensates for a change. Baseline records are not overwritten. The configured seed is used for the runs, helping compare variants under a consistent simulation setup.

The supplied simulator imposes observed recall counts, so changes in recall organization or category allocation are informative within that constraint. A sweep describes sensitivity over the chosen values; it does not establish that those values fit the data.

7 — Prepare sweeps and simultaneous interventions 
sweep_inputs = {}
base_figure_dir = resolve_project_path(figure_dir, root_path) if figure_dir is not None else output_dir
if set(parameter_sweeps) & set(parameter_interventions):
    raise ValueError("Sweep and intervention names must be distinct")
specifications = {}
for name, sweep in parameter_sweeps.items():
    values = sweep["values"]
    if not values or len(set(values)) != len(values):
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: supply distinct parameter values")
    specifications[name] = {
        "fit": sweep["fit"],
        "cases": [{"label": str(value), "stem": f"{sweep['parameter']}_{value}",
                   "overrides": {sweep["parameter"]: value}} for value in values],
    }
for name, intervention in parameter_interventions.items():
    if not intervention["overrides"]:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: supply at least one parameter override")
    specifications[name] = {
        "fit": intervention["fit"],
        "cases": [{"label": intervention.get("label", name), "stem": "intervention",
                   "overrides": intervention["overrides"]}],
    }
for name, specification in specifications.items():
    record = records[specification["fit"]]
    selection = selections[specification["fit"]]
    participant_ids = jnp.unique(data["subject"].ravel()[selection])
    params = parameters_for_subjects(record, participant_ids)
    for case in specification["cases"]:
        for key in case["overrides"]:
            if key not in params or key == "subject":
                raise ValueError(f"{name}: unknown or invalid parameter {key}")
    sweep_inputs[name] = {"fit_name": specification["fit"], "parameters": params,
                          "trial_mask": selection, "cases": specification["cases"]}
    print(name, "baseline:", specification["fit"], "interventions:", specification["cases"])
CMR_encoding baseline: CMR interventions: [{'label': '0.2', 'stem': 'encoding_drift_rate_0.2', 'overrides': {'encoding_drift_rate': 0.2}}, {'label': '0.5', 'stem': 'encoding_drift_rate_0.5', 'overrides': {'encoding_drift_rate': 0.5}}, {'label': '0.8', 'stem': 'encoding_drift_rate_0.8', 'overrides': {'encoding_drift_rate': 0.8}}]
eCMR_source_only_encoding baseline: eCMR_source_only interventions: [{'label': '0.2', 'stem': 'encoding_drift_rate_0.2', 'overrides': {'encoding_drift_rate': 0.2}}, {'label': '0.5', 'stem': 'encoding_drift_rate_0.5', 'overrides': {'encoding_drift_rate': 0.5}}, {'label': '0.8', 'stem': 'encoding_drift_rate_0.8', 'overrides': {'encoding_drift_rate': 0.8}}]
eCMR_broad_encoding baseline: eCMR_broad interventions: [{'label': '0.2', 'stem': 'encoding_drift_rate_0.2', 'overrides': {'encoding_drift_rate': 0.2}}, {'label': '0.5', 'stem': 'encoding_drift_rate_0.5', 'overrides': {'encoding_drift_rate': 0.5}}, {'label': '0.8', 'stem': 'encoding_drift_rate_0.8', 'overrides': {'encoding_drift_rate': 0.8}}]
temporal_emotional_modulation baseline: eCMR_broad interventions: [{'label': 'False', 'stem': 'phi_emot_modulates_temporal_False', 'overrides': {'phi_emot_modulates_temporal': False}}, {'label': 'True', 'stem': 'phi_emot_modulates_temporal_True', 'overrides': {'phi_emot_modulates_temporal': True}}]
8 — Simulate and save each baseline and intervention 
all_shifted_paths = {}
for sweep_name, prepared in sweep_inputs.items():
    model_name = prepared["fit_name"]
    fit_record = records[model_name]
    model_factory = construct_model(fit_record)
    loaded_features = load_features(fit_record)
    features = None if loaded_features is None else jnp.asarray(loaded_features)
    selected_trials = prepared["trial_mask"]
    paths = {}
    cases = [{"label": "Fitted baseline", "stem": "baseline", "overrides": {}}] + prepared["cases"]
    for case in cases:
        params = dict(prepared["parameters"])
        for key, value in case["overrides"].items():
            params[key] = jnp.full_like(params[key], value)
        simulated = simulate_dataset(
            model_factory, data, features, params, selected_trials,
            experiment_count=experiment_count,
            rng=jax.random.PRNGKey(simulation_seed),
            simulate_trial_fn=import_from_string(fit_record["simulation_function"]),
        )
        path = output_dir / sweep_name / (case["stem"] + ".h5")
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        save_dict_to_hdf5(simulated, str(path))
        metadata = {
            "baseline_fit_path": (fit_paths[model_name].relative_to(root_path).as_posix()
                                  if fit_paths[model_name].is_relative_to(root_path)
                                  else str(fit_paths[model_name])),
            "baseline_fits": fit_record["fits"],
            "applied_parameters": {key: np.asarray(value).tolist() for key, value in params.items()},
            "parameter_overrides": case["overrides"],
            "data_path": data_source,
            "selected_trial_indices": np.flatnonzero(np.asarray(selected_trials)).tolist(),
            "model_factory": fit_record["model_factory"], "components": fit_record["components"],
            "simulation_function": fit_record["simulation_function"],
            "embedding_path": fit_record.get("embedding_path", ""),
            "emotion_feature_path": fit_record.get("emotion_feature_path", ""),
            "feature_column": fit_record.get("feature_column", 6),
            "concat_features": fit_record.get("concat_features", False),
            "seed": simulation_seed, "experiment_count": experiment_count,
            "jaxcmr_version": jaxcmr.__version__, "jax_version": jax.__version__,
            "jax_enable_x64": enable_x64,
        }

        for key in ("embedding_path", "emotion_feature_path"):
            if metadata[key]:
                feature_path = resolve_project_path(metadata[key], root_path)
                metadata[key] = (feature_path.relative_to(root_path).as_posix()
                              if feature_path.is_relative_to(root_path) else str(feature_path))
        path.with_suffix(".json").write_text(json.dumps(metadata, indent=2) + "\n")
        paths[case["label"]] = str(path)
    all_shifted_paths[sweep_name] = paths

Compare intervention responses

Read the behavioral figures as contrasts against the unchanged baseline. Their patterns describe the selected lists and parameter values. You can add another configured analysis or reuse the saved response files in an analysis template.

9 — Prepare comparisons of saved sweep results 
comparison_groups = []
observed = data.copy()
if filter_repeated_recalls:
    observed["recalls"] = repetition.filter_repeated_recalls(observed["recalls"])
for sweep_name, paths in all_shifted_paths.items():
    sweep_figure_dir = base_figure_dir / sweep_name
    sweep_figure_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if not redo_figures:
        continue
    response_paths = [None, *paths.values()]  # None selects the observed responses.
    curve_labels = ["Observed", *paths.keys()]
    shared_settings = {
        "trial_mask": sweep_inputs[sweep_name]["trial_mask"],
        "figure_dir": sweep_figure_dir,
    }
    comparison_groups.append(
        {
            **shared_settings,
            "analyses": comparison_analysis_configs,
            "paths": response_paths,
            "labels": curve_labels,
            "suffix": "",
        }
    )
    for dataset_index, (path, label) in enumerate(zip(response_paths, curve_labels)):
        comparison_groups.append(
            {
                **shared_settings,
                "analyses": single_analysis_configs,
                "paths": [path],
                "labels": [label],
                "suffix": f"_single_{dataset_index}",
            }
        )
Code 
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
#| code-summary: "10 — Load one comparison at a time and plot its benchmarks"

for group in comparison_groups:
    analysis_configs = group["analyses"]
    if not analysis_configs:
        continue
    panel_data = []
    base_masks = []
    for path in group["paths"]:
        dataset = observed if path is None else load_data(path)
        if path is not None and filter_repeated_recalls:
            dataset["recalls"] = repetition.filter_repeated_recalls(dataset["recalls"])
        panel_data.append(dataset)
        base_masks.append(group["trial_mask"] if path is None else None)
    curve_labels = group["labels"]
    figure_dir = group["figure_dir"]
    for figure, figure_suffix in iter_analysis_figures(
        panel_data,
        analysis_configs,
        curve_labels,
        base_masks=base_masks,
        trial_query=analysis_trial_query,
        confidence_level=confidence_level,
        figure_size=figure_size,
        suffix=group["suffix"],
        bootstrap_seed=plot_seed,
    ):
        if figure_str:
            save_figure(
                str(figure_dir),
                figure_str,
                suffix=figure_suffix,
                formats=figure_formats,
                figure=figure,
            )
        else:
            figure.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
11 — Locate saved intervention responses 
for sweep_name, paths in all_shifted_paths.items():
    print(sweep_name, paths)

Reuse the results

The run saves baseline and intervention HDF5 responses with JSON simulation settings in the configured output folder, plus any requested behavioral figures. You can analyze these response files with other templates without repeating the sweep.

To investigate another mechanism, edit the named sweeps or simultaneous overrides, keep the baseline explicit, and choose a distinct output folder. Preserve the unchanged baseline when comparing interventions.
